title: Tabla comparativa de enfoques: Process Lasso, CPUSetSetter, el controlador de AMD y la API de conjuntos de CPU de Windows frente a Phynned, según el mecanismo, quién decide la colocación y si mide su propio efecto.
note: No row claims an advantage. Phynned has not been measured against any of these tools (the README's own comparison table is qualitative). Verification levels: V1 = primary source read first-hand on 2026-10-09; V3 = secondary press, primary not located.
options: Windows CPU Sets API (the mechanism itself)

cells: Affinity and CPU Sets dialogs; ProBalance lowers priority class of background processes
CPU Sets rather than affinity
Driver that changes which cores Windows prefers; a companion provisioning driver parks the second CCD
Soft affinity that cooperates with OS power management
Hard affinity and priority on admitted processes only (as implemented in 0.2.2); a CPU Sets lever is planned in the design docs, not built
Rules the user sets. ProBalance triggers on high system CPU load and lost responsiveness; the page gives no thresholds.
The user: rules are per program, core masks chosen by hand, with hotkeys to change or clear a mask on the fly.
Whether Windows sees a game. The reports disagree on the trigger (Game Mode, or Xbox Game Bar); AMD has not documented the internal logic in the sources found.
Whoever calls it. Not a policy.
A default-deny admission gate, then rules and profile, then user rules. A per-process A/B arbiter (cycles per unit of work) is designed and NOT built (MR-3).
Not described on the pages read. It logs which processes ProBalance acted on.
No built-in measurement described; its suggested approach is experimentation with hotkeys.
No.
n/a
A/B/A/B/A protocol exists for the operator to run; its exploratory catalog is provisional. The in-agent arbiter is unbuilt.
V1 for what the two pages say; the pages say nothing on whether the X3D cache CCD is detected or measured.
